title: The choice of the twists: Galois representations of lifts, Selmer groups made short by one anticyclotomic twist, and congruence bounds by Ribet's method
summary: For admissible data D and every prime ℓ with a fixed isomorphism ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ, the unit chooses weight-zero anticyclotomic twists ϑ for which the congruence bounds of a fit family hold (exists_isFitFamily): the ℓ-adic Galois representations attached to the forms of the auxiliary pairs are read as columns and rows (conjugate self-dual, with prescribed Hodge–Tate jumps, labelled by the tame characters at the chosen places), one anticyclotomic twist with tied auxiliary primes makes their Selmer groups short, and Ribet's method with congruent blocks gives a Hecke element whose valuation at the lift is within the budget, the crystalline losses above ℓ being affordable. Chunk 138-a holds the definitions (columns, rows, apt label tuples, the Selmer length bound, families of interpolated L-values, pencils of tied primes, balanced representations, even classes, blocks and the cocycles that obey relations), the existence of anticyclotomic characters at new primes, the Galois representations of labelled columns, and the crystalline defect at one place above ℓ.
chunk_title: Definitions of columns, rows and apt tuples; anticyclotomic characters at new primes; labelled columns; the crystalline defect at one place above ℓ
chunk_summary: Fifteen modules of New/Selmer, in import order from BlocksAndCocycles to OnePlaceDefect: the vocabulary of the unit (cocycles obeying relations, crystalline relations and the block loss, columns, rows, apt tuples, families, pencils, balanced representations, even classes, prime triangles), the construction of an anticyclotomic character of order ℓ^N at one new prime with prescribed Frobenius, families of values from integral measures, the passage from labelled columns to rows, a base level containing the image of the idempotent of apt labels, the spacing of thick places, and the local crystalline defect bounds.

members.name: obeyingCocycles
members.text: Let O be a commutative ring, G a group, σ and d finite types, X a type, u = (u_x)_{x∈X} a family of homomorphisms u_x : G → M_σ(O), ρ : G → M_d(O) a homomorphism and a ∈ O. obeyingCocycles u ρ a is the O-submodule of the functions c : G → (O/aO)^d (no continuity asked) such that (1) c is a cocycle for ρ: c(gh) = c(g) + ρ(g)·c(h) for all g, h ∈ G (the relations cocycleRels ρ), and (2) Σ_g θ(g)·c(g) = 0 for every finitely supported θ : G → O with Σ_g θ(g)·(u_x(g) − 1) = 0 in M_σ(O) for every x ∈ X.

members.name: obeyingCocycles.exists_graph_subrepresentation
members.text: Let O be a commutative Noetherian ring, G a group, X a finite type, σ and d finite types, u = (u_x)_{x∈X} homomorphisms u_x : G → M_σ(O), ρ : G → M_d(O) a homomorphism, a ∈ O, and c ∈ obeyingCocycles u ρ a. Let G act O-linearly on M = (M_σ(O))^X by g·(m_x)_x = (u_x(g)m_x)_x and on (O/aO)^d through ρ. Then there are k ∈ ℕ and a G-stable O-submodule Y of M × (O/aO)^d (a subrepresentation of the product representation) such that the first projection Y → M is injective and, for all g ∈ G and v ∈ M, ((u_x(g) − 1)_x + a^k·v, c(g)) ∈ Y. So c is, on the elements (u(g) − 1) + a^k v, the value of an equivariant map defined on the projection of Y, and Y is its graph (Artin–Rees).

members.name: IsFamily
members.text: For a stably unramified CM field E, a finite set S of finite places, a prime ℓ, an index type T, characters ν_i : Gal(Ω/E) → ℚ̄_ℓ^× (i ∈ T) and val assigning to a finite set I of places and a character χ : Gal(Ω/E) → ℚ̄_ℓ a value val(I, χ) ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ: IsFamily S ν val holds when (continuous_unitary) each ν_i is continuous; (exists_interp) for every I auxiliary for S there are a finite type α, elements g_a ∈ Gal(Ω/E) and c_a ∈ ℚ̄_ℓ with ‖c_a‖ ≤ 1 such that val(I, χ) = Σ_a c_a·χ(g_a) for every χ; (val_insert_le) for every I, every P ∉ I with I ∪ {P} auxiliary for S, every χ from U(1) for the places above ℓ with modulus I (IsFromU1), every place A over P, every arithmetic Frobenius φ at A for q_P and every c ≥ 0: if v_ℓ(1 − ν_i(φ)·χ(φ)^{±1}) ≤ c for all i and both signs, then v_ℓ(val(I ∪ {P}, χ)) ≤ v_ℓ(val(I, χ)) + 8c (v_ℓ = ellVal); (val_empty_ne_zero) val(∅, 1) ≠ 0.

members.name: exists_isAnticyclotomicAt
members.text: Let E₁ be a stably unramified CM field embedded in Ω, ℓ' a prime, N ∈ ℕ, S a finite set of finite places of E₁, R a finite set of finite places, z ∈ Gal(Ω/E₁) an element of the normal closure of the inertia above the places of R that are not in S ∪ S̄ and not above ℓ' (the smallest normal subgroup containing the union of those inertia groups: a weaker hypothesis than membership in the union itself, which is what the twist theorem's hypothesis hz asks for), and W a neighbourhood of z. Then there is a finite place P ∉ R ∪ R̄ of prime norm and there are auxiliary prime data l = (A, γ, φ, h) with h : Gal(Ω/E₁) → ℤ/ℓ'^N (into the multiplicative copy Multiplicative (ZMod (ℓ'^N))) such that φ ∈ W, h(φ) = 0 in ℤ/ℓ'^N (Lean's l.h l.φ = 1: the identity of the multiplicative copy, not the generator ofAdd 1 that IsAnticyclotomicAt prescribes at the tame generator γ; for N = 0 the target ℤ/1 is trivial), and IsAnticyclotomicAt T P l for every T ⊆ S ∪ (places above ℓ').

members.name: IsPrimeTriangle
members.text: For a prime ℓ, ν ∈ ℕ, a stably unramified CM field E, a finite linearly ordered index type J, places w_j, elements τ_j, φ_j, a ∈ Gal(Ω/E), t ∈ ℕ, a monotone map ty : J → {e ∈ Fin t : 0 < e} (the twist served by w_j) and h, c ∈ ℕ: IsPrimeTriangle ν w τ φ a t ty h c holds when (isNewPlaces) IsNewPlaces ν w τ φ; (detect) there is a finite set s ⊆ Gal(Ω/E) with (|J| + |s|)·h ≤ c such that for every coefficient ring O and every e, a cocycle z in the Selmer module of O(−e) modulo ℓ^ν unramified outside the places above ℓ that vanishes on s is zero; (prod_dvd) for every e < t, ∏_{k ≠ e} (cyc(a⁻¹)^e − cyc(a⁻¹)^k) divides ℓ^h in ℤ_ℓ; (step) for every O and j, every z ∈ evenClasses O (range w) ν (ty_j) with z(τ_i) = 0, and z(φ_i) = 0 whenever ty_i = ty_j, for all i < j, has ℓ^h·z(τ_j) = 0; (coboundary) for every O and every 0 < e < t, with d(g) = cycInv(g)^e − 1 in O: 4·d(a)² divides ℓ^h in O, and every z ∈ evenClasses O ∅ ν e with z(φ_j) = 0 for all j with ty_j = e satisfies d(a)·(2z)(g) = d(g)·(2z)(a) for all g.

members.text: For a prime ℓ, a stably unramified CM field E, a ring O of integers of a finite extension of ℚ_ℓ (PadicIntegerRing O ℓ), a finite type n, a finite set S of finite places, ρ : Gal(Ω/E) → M_n(O), a set L of relations, γ ∈ Gal(Ω/E), β and M: IsBalanced ℓ S ρ L γ β M holds when (isLocallyConstant) ρ modulo ℓ^M is locally constant; (unramified) ρ(g) = 1 for every g in the inertia above the places off S; (span_eq_top) the O-span of ρ(Gal(Ω/E)) is all of M_n(O); (scalar_inertia) γ lies in the inertia above the places of S not above ℓ, and there is s ∈ O with ρ((γ^c)⁻¹) = s·1, ρ(γ) = s·1, and s + 1, s − 1 units of O; (lt_card_residue) 4|n| + 2 < |O/𝔪_O|; (coboundary_mem) for every a ∈ O and b ∈ (O/a)^n, the coboundary g ↦ ρ(g)b − b obeys L; (local_length_le) there are g ∈ Gal(Ω/E) and α, α' ∈ O with ρ(g) = α·1 and ρ((g^c)⁻¹) = α'·1 such that for every a dividing ℓ^M: Σ_{v∈S} min_{A over v} length_O(localCocycles ρ L A (O/a)) + |n|·v_O(α − cyc(g^c)·α') ≤ (|S| + f_E)·length_O((O/a)^n) + β, f_E the number of infinite places of E and v_O the additive valuation of O.

members.name: crystalline_defect_le
members.text: Local loss, crystalline case. Let ℓ be a prime, Γ a topological group over G_ℓ (GroupOverGp: j = Γ.overGp.toGp : Γ → G_ℓ with open image), O a coefficient ring, L a Galois lattice over O for Γ, Q, m, h, μ, G, b, δ, η, W natural numbers, th and ε functions of the ℤ_ℓ-algebra embeddings g : O → ℂ_ℓ (a thickness indicator and a sign), and U(g), U'(g) finite sets of integers, such that: Q > 0; 99(Q² + (W + 1)Q + Q + W + m) ≤ h; 99h³ ≤ G; 99(Gh³ + G) ≤ b; 2 log(4b) < m; δ < η; 99((η + W)Q + η + h) ≤ h³; for every g, U(g) ⊆ [−η, η] ∪ (−ε(g))·[β_g, β_g + W] and U'(g) ⊆ [−η, η] ∪ ε(g)·[β_g, β_g + W] with β_g = b + δ if th(g) and G + δ otherwise (IsInJumpWindow); L lies in the class InClass ⊤ ⊥ U' (crystalline lattices with jumps in U'); either (for every g, every negative u in U(g) ∪ U'(g) has 2u ≤ −h, and the number of jumps of L at g in [−η, η] is at most μ) or (every U'(g) ⊆ [−η, 0]); y ≥ 0 with 10⁵·(rk_O L·⌊2λ/Q⌋·m + μ·λ) ≤ y, λ = lambdaLoss h b ℓ; k a Kummer chart of Γ with a root ζ ∈ O of the letters (ζ^{ℓ^f − 1} = 1), T and s functions on O, j an open embedding (hj), e·f = [G_ℓ : j(Γ)] for the chart (hf), e ≤ h (he); for every g with th(g) or Q < ℓ, th(g) = T(g(ζ)) and ε(g) = s(g(ζ)) (hs); either (the chart is unramified and ℓ ≥ 7) or (ℓ ≤ Q and s is constant) (hu); and, if ℓ ≤ Q, for every z and 1 ≤ a, a' ≤ log_ℓ(h³), T(z) and T(z^{ℓ^a}) imply ¬T(z^{ℓ^{a+a'}}) (hT). Then the normalised O-length of Z_f(L) modulo Z_f(L) ∩ cupOrthogonal (InClass ⊤ ⊥ U) L is at most [G_ℓ : j(Γ)]·y.

members.text: Mirror lemma. Let O be a commutative ring, G a group, n a finite type, I an ideal of O with O/I finite, ρ : G → M_n(O) a homomorphism whose O-span is all of M_n(O) (hρ), χ : G → O a homomorphism, c an endomorphism of G with c(c(g)) = g (_hc), H and U subgroups of G with H normal, γ, g₀, z ∈ G, s ∈ O, y : G → (O/I)^n, a type W and additive maps x_w(g) : (O/I)^n → ℚ/ℤ (w ∈ W, g ∈ G), such that: (hi) w is determined by the restriction of x_w to U; (hU) ρ(g) acts trivially on (O/I)^n for g ∈ U; (hH) c(H) ⊆ H and H ⊆ U; (κ) every commutator [g, γ] lies in H; (p, s₂) s − 1 and s + 1 are units; (hγ) ρ((cγ)⁻¹) = s·1, ρ(γ) = s·1, χ(cγ) = χ(γ) = 1 and y(γ) = 0; (hz) z ∈ U and c(z) ∈ U; (hy) y is a cocycle, y(gh) = y(g) + ρ(g)·y(h); (hu) some coordinate y(g₀)_i is a unit; (hW) x_w(a·g b g⁻¹)(m) = x_w(a)(m) + x_w(b)(χ(g)·ρ(g)⁻¹·m) for a, b ∈ U; (hq) x_w(zh)(t·y(zh)) = x_w(c(zh))(t·y(c(zh))) for h ∈ H and t ∈ O (isotropy on the coset zH); and (hδ) ρ(g) = α·1 and ρ((cg)⁻¹) = α'·1. Then |W| is at most the number of m ∈ (O/I)^n with (α − χ(cg)·α')·m = 0.

For a prime ℓ, a stably unramified CM field E, finite sets S ⊆ S₀ of finite places of E (hS), an element z of Gal(Ω/E) in the inertia above the places of S₀ not above ℓ (hz: z ∈ inertiaAbove(S₀ ∖ placesDividing(E, ℓ)), the union of the inertia groups of the places of Ω over these places), representations ρ_i (i ∈ ι, finite) over a coefficient ring O balanced up to β_i (hρ: IsBalanced ℓ S ρ_i L_i γ_i β_i M), finite types κ, T, families (μ_k, val_k) with IsFamily S₀ (μ_k) (val_k) for each k ∈ κ (hf), bounds B_i < ∞ (hB) with normLength(β_i + Σ_b v(det(ρ_i(z_b) − 1))) ≤ B_i, z_b ∈ {z, (z^c)⁻¹} (hβ), c, η ≥ 0 with v_ℓ(μ_{k,t}(z) − 1) ≤ c for all k, t (hc), η > 0 (hη), and m ∈ ℕ: there are a finite set I of places and a character ψ : Gal(Ω/E) → ℚ̄_ℓ such that for every 1 ≤ d ≤ m: (1) for every k, v_ℓ(val_k(I, ψ^d)) ≤ v_ℓ(val_k(∅, 1)) + 8c + η; (2) IsAuxTwist S₀ I ψ^d η; and (3) for every i and all sufficiently large coefficient rings O' ⊇ O, some ψ' with values in O' agreeing with ψ^d gives normLength_{O'}(length of the Selmer module of ψ'·ρ_i for the places S ∪ I ∪ Ī, relations L_i ∪ {vanishing at γ_i}, modulo ℓ^M) ≤ B_i + η.

members.text: For an O-subalgebra S of the functions Y → L[X_J] and an S-submodule 𝒥 of them, a finite J, β : Y → L, a subset 𝓧 ⊆ Y, a point π ∈ 𝓧 and c ∈ L: IsRibetElement 𝒥 β π c holds when the function x ↦ β(x) (as constant polynomials) lies in S and some f ∈ S has f·β ∈ 𝒥, with β(x) = 0 and the coefficient in f(x) of every monomial X^d with d < 1_J (1_J = Σ_j single(j, 1), the all-ones multi-index) in the pointwise order of multi-indices — that is, of every monomial properly dividing the squarefree product ∏_j X_j; a monomial of smaller total degree such as X_1² (when |J| = 3) is not concerned — equal to 0 for every x ∈ 𝓧, and the coefficient of ∏_j X_j in f(π) equal to c.

members.name: ribet_first_order
members.text: Ribet's lemma to first order. Let O be a discrete valuation ring, L an O-algebra, Y and J finite (J linearly ordered), G a group, u_x : G → M_σ(O) (x ∈ Y), S ⊆ (Y → L[X_J]) an O-subalgebra and 𝒥 an S-submodule; r finite, t ≥ 1, ϵ : r ⊕ Fin t ≃ σ; 𝓧 ⊆ Y, π ∈ 𝓧, ρ_x : G → M_r(O) (x ∈ 𝓧) and characters ξ_e : G → O (e < t) with ξ_0 = 1 (ξ₀), such that on 𝓧, u_x is the block sum of ρ_x and diag(ξ_e) reindexed by ϵ (hu); ρ_π spans M_r(O) (hρ); γ_x ∈ G, y_x ∈ O with ρ_x(γ_x) = y_x·1 (h₀), y_x − 1 a unit (hy), ξ_e(γ_x) = 1 (hγ); p ≠ 0 (hp); IsTraceIdeal 𝒥 u p τ φ (first projection) ε (h𝒥); p ∣ ε_{k.1}(ξ_e(φ_k)) − 1 (hε); a ∈ G with ∏_{k≠e}(ξ_e(a) − ξ_k(a)) ∣ C for every e (hC); ty : J → Fin t monotone; p₀ ≠ 0 (hp₀); β(x) = det(Σ_g n_g·(u_x(g) − 1)) for the combination ribetNormaliser γ_π a y_π (p₀C) n (hβ); b₀ < v(p₀) (hlt); the length of the cocycles in obeyingCocycles u ρ_π p₀ vanishing at the τ's and at γ_π is ≤ b₀ (hb₀); W finite, δ_v ∈ G and polynomials o_v with ξ_e(δ_v) = 1 (hδ) and (o_v·(X − 1))(u_x(δ_v)) = 0 (hH); and, for every e and every module Z of cocycles obeying (u, ξ_e) modulo p, vanishing at the δ_v, whose coboundary-like elements are killed by ξ_e(a) − 1: HasTriangleCost Z τ φ {j : ty j = e} C (b e), and the elements of Z vanishing on a finite set s are zero (hb). Then there is c ∈ O with IsRibetElement 𝒥 β π (c read in L) and v(c) ≤ b₀ + (Σ_e b_e + t·(Σ_v v(o_v(1)) + 2|s|·v(C)) + (|J| + 1)·v(C)).

members.name: obeyingCocycles.mem_selmerModule
members.text: Let ℓ be a prime, D admissible data for parameters P with field E = D.E, Y, n and r finite types and O a coefficient ring (the ring of integers of a finite Galois extension of ℚ_ℓ inside ℚ̄_ℓ). Let u = (u_x)_{x∈Y} be a family of homomorphisms u_x : Gal(Ω/E) → M_n(O) into the multiplicative monoid of n×n matrices, each continuous (hc); let S be a set of finite places of E such that u_x(g) = 1 for every x ∈ Y and every g in the inertia above a place of E outside S (hS); let ρ : Gal(Ω/E) → M_r(O) be a homomorphism, b ∈ O with b ≠ 0 (NeZero b), c : Gal(Ω/E) → (O/bO)^r a function and L a set of relations (finitely supported functions Gal(Ω/E) → M_r(O)). If c ∈ obeyingCocycles u ρ b (h: c is a cocycle for ρ modulo b, continuous or not, with Σ_g θ(g)c(g) = 0 for every finitely supported θ : Gal(Ω/E) → O such that Σ_g θ(g)(u_x(g) − 1) = 0 for all x) and c obeys L (l: c ∈ obeying L (O/bO)), then c lies in the Selmer module selmerModule ρ S L (O/bO): c is a locally constant cocycle for ρ, vanishes on the inertia above every place outside S, and obeys L.

If IsTraceIdeal (for S and ℚ̄_ℓ) 𝒥 (x, g ↦ u_x(g)) (ℓ^ν) τ φ id e holds (h), then IsTraceIdeal 𝒥 (x, g ↦ u_x(g)) (ℓ^ν) (withConjInv τ) (withConjInv φ) (k, b ↦ k) e holds: the family indexed by K × Bool with values τ_k at (k, true) and (τ_k^c)⁻¹ at (k, false) (and likewise for φ), with the same variable X_k for both copies of k. members.name: IsLaw
members.text: For a prime ℓ, a stably unramified CM field E embedded in Ω, r ∈ ℕ, e ∈ ℕ, a set Φ ⊆ Gal(Ω/E), a finite set T of finite places of the maximal real subfield E⁺ and a function z : Gal(Ω/E) → ℤ/ℓ^r: IsLaw r e Φ T z (a reciprocity law of twist e + 1 against the even classes of twist −e that vanish on Φ, with exceptional set T) holds when (isLocallyConstant) z is locally constant; (map_conj_mul) for all g, a, b ∈ Gal(Ω/E) with cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) a = 1 and cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) b = 1: z(g a g⁻¹ b) = (cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) g)^{e+1}·z(a) + z(b); (odd) for every b ∈ Gal(Ω/E) with cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^r) b = 1: z(b^c) = −z(b), b^c = conjGal(b); (reciprocity) for every finite type J and every family x : J → FrobeniusDatum E, x_j = (w_j, A_j, s_j), such that the places primeBelowPlus w_j of E⁺ are pairwise distinct and, for every j, IsSplitPlace r x_j holds and primeBelowPlus w_j ∉ T: for every j ∈ J with z(s_i) = 0 for all i ≠ j, every coefficient ring O, every c ∈ evenClasses O {w_i : i ∈ J} r e with c(g) = 0 for all g ∈ Φ, and every n ∈ ℕ such that 2·z(s_j) divides n in ℤ/ℓ^r: n·c(τ_j) = 0, where τ_j is the chosen generator of tame inertia at the place A_j over w_j (the tameGenerator of x_j's place).

members.name: exists_isPrimeTriangle
members.text: For a prime ℓ (ThePrime ℓ), a CM number field E that is stably unramified and embedded in Ω (Field E, UnramCMField E), natural numbers t, N, y, h with N ≠ 0 (NeZero N), an element γ ∈ Gal(Ω/E) and a set W of Frobenius data of E, suppose: (hE) the image of E in Ω lies in the cyclotomic field cycloField N = ℚ(ζ_N); (hN) N + t < y; (hh) for every natural number a with 0 < a < t, (cycChar Ω ℓ γ)^a − 1 divides ℓ^h in ℤ_ℓ (cycChar Ω ℓ is the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character of Gal(Ω/E), with values in ℤ_ℓ^×); (hy) ℓ ≤ y² or h = 0; (hf) numInfPlaces E ≥ 4 (E has at least four infinite places); (hW) for every ν ∈ ℕ and every g ∈ Gal(Ω/E) there is δ ∈ Gal(Ω/E) with cycChar Ω ℓ δ = 1 such that W ∈ mostFrobeniiAt E (δ^{ℓ^ν}·g), i.e. W belongs to the filter mostFrobenii E ⊓ comap (x ↦ x.frob) (𝓝(δ^{ℓ^ν}·g)) on Frobenius data (a set belongs to mostFrobenii E when every nonempty open subset of Gal(Ω/E) contains a nonempty open set U such that, for all but finitely many places w of E of prime norm, every Frobenius datum (w, A, s) with s ∈ U lies in it). Then there are a type J, a Fintype structure and a linear order on J, and a monotone map ty : J → {e ∈ Fin t : 0 < e}, such that for every ν > 0 there are Taylor–Wiles places Q : TaylorWilesPlaces E J (ℓ^ν) — Frobenius data x_j = Q.frobData j (j ∈ J), each consisting of a finite place w_j = Q.w j of E of prime norm q_j, a place A_j of Ω over w_j and a geometric Frobenius x_j.frob at A_j, such that j ↦ w_j is injective and w̄_i ≠ w_j for all i, j (IsConjApart (j ↦ w_j)), and ℓ^ν divides q_j − 1 for every j — with (1) IsPrimeTriangle ν Q.w τ φ γ⁻¹ t ty (y·h) (y²²·h), where τ_j is the chosen tame generator at A_j (x_j.isPlaceOver.tameGenerator) and φ_j = x_j.frob, and (2) x_j ∈ W for every j ∈ J. Unfolded, (1) says: (isNewPlaces) IsNewPlaces ν Q.w τ φ: for every j, w_j is not above ℓ, φ_j acts trivially on the ℓ^ν-th roots of unity (cycCharMod Ω (ℓ^ν) φ_j = 1), and τ_j is the chosen tame generator at some place of Ω over w_j; (detect) there is a finite set s ⊆ Gal(Ω/E) with (|J| + |s|)·(y·h) ≤ y²²·h such that for every coefficient ring O (CoeffRing ℓ) and every e ∈ ℕ, every cocycle z ∈ selmerModule (tateTwist ℓ E O e) (placesDividing E ℓ) ∅ (QuotSpan (ℓ^ν)) (a locally constant cocycle Gal(Ω/E) → O/ℓ^ν for the character g ↦ cycInv ℓ E O g^e, unramified outside the places above ℓ) that vanishes on s is zero; (prod_dvd) for every e ∈ Fin t, ∏_{k ∈ Fin t, k ≠ e}((cycChar Ω ℓ (γ⁻¹)⁻¹)^e − (cycChar Ω ℓ (γ⁻¹)⁻¹)^k), that is ∏_{k ≠ e}((cycChar Ω ℓ γ)^e − (cycChar Ω ℓ γ)^k), divides ℓ^{y·h} in ℤ_ℓ; (step) for every O, every j ∈ J and every z ∈ evenClasses O (range Q.w) ν (ty j) such that for all i < j, z(τ_i) = 0 and (ty i = ty j ⇒ z(φ_i) = 0): ℓ^{y·h}·z(τ_j) = 0; (coboundary) for every O and every e ∈ {e ∈ Fin t : 0 < e}, writing d(g) = cycInv ℓ E O g^e − 1: 2²·d(γ⁻¹)² divides ℓ^{y·h} in O, and every z ∈ evenClasses O ∅ ν e with z(φ_j) = 0 for all j with ty j = e satisfies d(γ⁻¹)·(z + z)(g) = d(g)·(z + z)(γ⁻¹) for all g ∈ Gal(Ω/E). Here evenClasses O S ν e is the set of the cocycles c ∈ selmerModule (tateTwist ℓ E O e) (placesDividing E ℓ ∪ S ∪ S̄) ∅ (QuotSpan (ℓ^ν)) that are even (c(g^c) = c(g) for all g, g^c the conjugate by complex conjugation) and vanish on shaLocalSet ℓ E 1 (the elements of the decomposition groups above ℓ with trivial cyclotomic character).

members.name: denominatorLe_rowBudget
members.text: Let P be parameters, D admissible data for P with CM field E = D.E, ℓ a prime (ThePrime ℓ) and ι an element of the class PadicIso ℓ, i.e. a ring isomorphism ιℓ : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ. Let ϑ be a twist of D (D.Twist: a character of U(1)(𝔸_E) of weight 0 whose tame part is trivial off a finite set Q = ϑ.Q of finite places, Q disjoint from its conjugate, the norms of Q prime to g₀g₁N, and the tame part non-trivial at every place of Q), ψ = ϑ.invAvatar the ℓ-adic avatar through ιℓ of (the base change to E of) ϑ⁻¹, a character Gal(Ω/E) → ℚ̄_ℓ, and suppose (hq) IsAuxTwist (badPlaces D ℓ) ϑ.Q ψ (crudeUnit ℓ D): ϑ.Q is auxiliary for the set badPlaces D ℓ of places of E dividing ℓ·g₀g₁·N (every v ∈ ϑ.Q has prime norm, v, v̄ ∉ badPlaces D ℓ and v̄ ∉ ϑ.Q), ψ is from U(1) with modulus ϑ.Q for the places above ℓ (IsFromU1: locally constant and ψ(Art x) = η(x/x̄) for an idele character η of that modulus), and there are elements σ_P (P ∈ ϑ.Q) with IsNewPlaces 0 (ϑ.Q ↪ places) σ 1 (each σ_P the chosen tame generator at a place of Ω over P, P not above ℓ) and Σ_{P∈ϑ.Q} v_ℓ(ψ(σ_P) − 1) ≤ crudeUnit ℓ D = v_ℓ(Mk) + 2^{−ℓ} (v_ℓ = ellVal, the valuation of ℚ̄_ℓ normalised by v_ℓ(ℓ) = 1, Mk = D.chosenGroupOrder). Let r, n be finite types, O an auxiliary pair over E of ranks (|r|, |n|) (forms on V = I_n: O.FormV), e₀ an element of the complex group algebra of the finite group ∏_{w chosen place of O} GL_{|r|}(k_w) (Lean names it E; it is not the field), and Z a complex subspace of the forms on V. Suppose (hw) that Z is contained in the complex span of the set A of the y ∈ Z such that (a) there are labels c at the chosen places of O with y ∈ im(tupleProj O c), IsApt O c ϑ, and im(tupleProj O c) ⊆ im(AuxPair.groupAlgAction O e₀); and (b) there is a family z of Hecke eigenvalues with AuxPair.Lifts O y z, and there are an ℓ-adic representation R : Gal(Ω/E) → GL_{|r|}(ℚ̄_ℓ) and an auxiliary pair V over E of ranks (|r|, |n|) with HasRow V z R, O.μ = V.μ · ϑ.toAutChar (the characters of the pairs), and elements γ ∈ Gal(Ω/E), s in the integers of ℚ̄_ℓ with SelmerLengthLe ψ R ϑ.Q (⌊D.r · rowBudget D ℓ⌋₊ + 1) γ s. Then DenominatorLe ιℓ O e₀ Z (rowBudget D ℓ · log ℓ) holds: for d = dim_ℂ Z and all families y, y' : {0, …, d − 1} → forms on V such that every y_a is integral at every ring homomorphism j : ℂ → ℂ_ℓ (y_a ∈ integralForms j) and every y'_b is integral at the homomorphism ℂ → ℂ_ℓ given by ιℓ followed by ℚ̄_ℓ ⊆ ℂ_ℓ and satisfies AuxPair.IsTested O e₀ Z^⊥ y'_b (for every finite place w of E with w̄ ≠ w and w not among the places of O and their conjugates, y'_b is orthogonal to im(AuxPair.groupAlgAction O e₀) ∩ ker(AuxPair.heckePolyOnForms O hw hS (AuxPair.testValue O w)) ∩ Z^⊥): ‖ιℓ(det(⟨y_a, pr_Z y'_b⟩)_{a,b})‖ ≤ exp(d · (|r| · rowBudget D ℓ · log ℓ)), where pr_Z is the orthogonal projection onto Z and ⟨·,·⟩ the inner product of forms on V. In words: the ℓ-adic denominator of the projection to a space spanned by lifts with short Selmer groups is at most |r|·rowBudget D ℓ per dimension, without any bound for the even classes.

members.text: Let E be a field with a CM type and Weil data, r and n finite types, O an auxiliary pair over E with index types r ⊂ n, σ an automorphism of the field ℂ, φ and φ' forms in O.FormV (algebraic forms on V = I_n of the weight, level and character of O), w a finite place of E with w̄ ≠ w (hw), such that neither w (hS) nor w̄ (hS') lies in the set of places of O and their conjugates, and X ∈ ℂ. Let c be labels at the chosen places of O that are apt for the trivial twist (IsApt O c 1, hO), b a family of eigenvalues (for every finite place w of E a sequence b(w) of complex numbers), J jumps (a multiset J(σ) of integers for every complex embedding σ of E), and R : Gal(Ω/E) → GL_r(ℚ̄_ℓ) an ℓ-adic representation of rank |r| with: (h) R is a labelled column IsLabelledColumn O |r| J c ∅ R (R is a conjugate self-dual column of jumps J, empty extra level, and at each chosen place of O inertia is killed through the tame characters given by the roots of c); (s) for every g ∈ Gal(Ω/E), ιℓ(b(x.w)(1)) tends to tr R(g) along the Frobenius data x = (w, A, s) with s approaching g (mostFrobeniiAt); (hJ) the shifted jumps σ ↦ {u − ((|r| − O.rankDiff)/2 − cmSign(σ)·weight_μ(σ)) : u ∈ J(σ)} (weight_μ the weight of the character μ of O at the place of σ; the half-difference (|r| − O.rankDiff)/2 is taken in ℤ — |r| − O.rankDiff is a difference of integers, possibly negative, not a truncated subtraction of natural numbers, and it is even, |r| and O.rankDiff being odd) satisfy IsRowType D |r| O.rankDiff. Then there is an ℓ-adic representation T of rank |r| with HasRow O b T: T is a row (IsRow D O.rankDiff τ T for some jumps τ), and for every tame character ϑ of D, every auxiliary pair V over E(D) with index types r ⊂ n and character V.μ = O.μ·ϑ, every form y on V lifting b (V.Lifts y b), every Hecke system H for which y is an eigenform (IsEigenform y H), every representation S attached to H (Attached H S) and every g ∈ Gal(Ω/E): tr(normalisedRep V S (g)) = ϑ.invAvatar(g)·tr T(g) + Σ_{0≤e<V.rankDiff} cyc⁻¹(g)^e, where normalisedRep V S is S twisted by the character chiOneInv V and cyc⁻¹ = cycInv is the inverse ℓ-adic cyclotomic character. (The statement uses ιℓ, so Lean also takes the section variables {ℓ}, [ThePrime ℓ] and (ι : PadicIso ℓ), which the line census does not list: a prime ℓ and a fixed ring isomorphism ιℓ : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ; to be confirmed with #check.)

members.name: exists_mFoldTwist_selmerLengthLe
members.text: Let P be parameters, D admissible data for P, ℓ a prime with a fixed ring isomorphism ιℓ : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ (ι : PadicIso ℓ), I a finite index type, r_i (i ∈ I) finite types and R_i : Gal(Ω/E) → GL_{r_i}(ℚ̄_ℓ) ℓ-adic representations each of which is a row (h: for every i there are t and jumps J with IsRow D t J R_i), and M a natural number. Then there is an m-fold twist τ of D such that for every n with 1 ≤ n ≤ m, writing ϑ = τ^n (τ.powTwist n), Q = Q(ϑ) its set of places and ψ = ϑ.invAvatar (the ℓ-adic avatar through ιℓ of the base change of ϑ⁻¹, a character Gal(Ω/E) → ℚ̄_ℓ): (1) IsAuxTwist (badPlaces D ℓ) Q ψ (crudeUnit ℓ D): Q is auxiliary for badPlaces D ℓ (every v ∈ Q has prime norm, v and v̄ lie outside badPlaces D ℓ, v̄ ∉ Q), ψ comes from U(1) for the places above ℓ with modulus Q (IsFromU1: locally constant, ψ(Art x) = η(x/x̄) for a character η of the finite ideles trivial on E^× and on the ideles that are units off ℓ and its conjugates and principal units at the places of Q), and there are σ_v (v ∈ Q), each the chosen tame generator at a place of Ω over v (IsNewPlaces 0 (Q ↪ places) σ 1), with Σ_{v∈Q} v_ℓ(ψ(σ_v) − 1) ≤ cr_ℓ; (2) for every i there are γ ∈ Gal(Ω/E) and y in the integers of ℚ̄_ℓ with SelmerLengthLe ψ R_i Q M γ y (for all sufficiently large coefficient rings O: a lattice of ψ·R_i on which γ acts by the scalar y with y − 1 a unit and cyc(γ) = 1, and the Selmer module of that lattice modulo ℓ^M — continuous cocycles unramified off the places above ℓ, g₀g₁ and Q ∪ Q̄, obeying the crystalline relations crysRels above ℓ — intersected with {c : c(γ) = 0} has normalised length at most (10·f·|r_i| + 1)·cr_ℓ); (3) for every pair p of D and every sign s ∈ ℤˣ, if p is ramified then ‖ιℓ(ratio(p, ϑ, s)⁻¹)‖ ≤ exp(9·cr_ℓ·log ℓ). Here cr_ℓ = crudeUnit ℓ D = v_ℓ(Mk) + 2^{−ℓ}, Mk = chosenGroupOrder, v_ℓ the ℓ-adic valuation normalised by v_ℓ(ℓ) = 1, and ratio(p, ϑ, s) = |L(z, (νϑ^s)⁻¹)|/|L(z, ν⁻¹)| for p = (ν, z).

lemma exists_mFoldTwist_selmerLengthLe {P} (D : Data P) ℓ [ThePrime ℓ] (ι : PadicIso ℓ) {I : Type}
    [Finite I] {r : I → Type} [∀ i, Fintype (r i)] {R : ∀ i, _ →* GL (r i)
    _} (h : ∀ i, ∃ t J, IsRow D t J (R i)) M : ∃ τ : D.MFoldTwist, ∀ n, let ϑ := τ.powTwist n
  IsAuxTwist (badPlaces D ℓ) ϑ.Q ϑ.invAvatar (crudeUnit ℓ D) ∧
    (∀ i, ∃ γ y, SelmerLengthLe ϑ.invAvatar (R i) ϑ.Q M γ y) ∧
    ∀ (p : D.Pair) s, p.IsRamified → ‖ιℓ (p.ratio ϑ s)⁻¹‖ ≤ exp (9 * crudeUnit ℓ D * log ℓ)

members.name: exists_isFitFamily
members.text: For all parameters P and all admissible data D for P there is a family θ = (θ_{ℓ,ι}) of m-fold twists of D (θ : PrimePadicIso → D.MFoldTwist), one for each prime ℓ and each ring isomorphism ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ, with D.IsFitFamily θ — the whole family θ is chosen before j, the rank-one pair and the sign are quantified, and θ_{ℓ,ι} may depend on ι at fixed ℓ — that is: (coprime) for every pair (ℓ, ι) of a prime ℓ and a ring isomorphism ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_ℓ, ℓ is coprime to the product N(Q(θ_{ℓ,ι})) of the norms of the places of the set Q of the twist θ_{ℓ,ι}; (denominator_le) for every j with 1 ≤ j ≤ m there is γ : ℕ → ℝ with Σ_{ℓ∈T} γ(ℓ) ≤ B₀(D) = f·a·(log b)³/(m·k) for every finite set T of primes, such that for every (ℓ, ι) (the same γ(ℓ) at every ι over ℓ and for both families below): DenominatorLe ι (auxPair D θ_{ℓ,ι}^j j) e₀(D) (image of D.goodLift θ_{ℓ,ι}^j j) γ(ℓ) — the orthogonal projection onto the lifts θ_j^* of the good forms on W_j at the twist θ_{ℓ,ι}^j has ℓ-adic denominator at most γ(ℓ) per unit of rank and dimension, in the sense of DenominatorLe (for every d = dim Z and all families y, y' of d forms on V_j with every y_a integral at every embedding ℂ → ℂ_ℓ and every y'_b integral at ι and tested for e₀(D) and Z^⊥: ‖ι(det(⟨y_a, pr_Z y'_b⟩))‖ ≤ exp(d·|r|·γ(ℓ)), Z the image of the good lift) — and for every pair p of D of rank one for j (H : p.IsRankOne j), DenominatorLe ι Y.auxPair (tupleIdem (i ↦ X − 1)) (ℂ·Y.trivialLift) γ(ℓ) with Y = p.lValueData H.1 θ_{ℓ,ι}^j, the L-value data of p twisted by θ_{ℓ,ι}^j; here θ_{ℓ,ι}^j = (θ_{ℓ,ι}).powTwist j; and (height_le) for every j with 1 ≤ j ≤ m, every pair p of D and every sign s ∈ ℤˣ: if p is ramified (its tame part is non-trivial exactly at the chosen places), the family (ℓ, ι) ↦ ratio(p, θ_{ℓ,ι}^j, s)⁻¹ has height at most x^999 (HeightLe: there are H ≠ 0 and reals α, e(ℓ) with |σ(H)| ≤ exp α for every automorphism σ of ℂ, ‖ι(H·ratio(p, θ_{ℓ,ι}^j, s)⁻¹)‖ ≤ exp e(ℓ) for every (ℓ, ι), and α + Σ_{primes ℓ<M} e(ℓ) ≤ x^999 for all large M — one multiplier H for every embedding), ratio(p, ϑ, s) = |L(z, (νϑ^s)⁻¹)|/|L(z, ν⁻¹)| with the Euler factors removed at the conjugate closure of the chosen places in the denominator and at the conjugate closure of (the chosen places ∪ Q(ϑ)) in the numerator (AutChar.L S removes the Euler factors at S ∪ S̄). An m-fold twist is a twist whose tame part ψ has ψ_w^n ≠ 1 for every w in its set Q and 1 ≤ n ≤ m: its powers 1, …, m all stay ramified on the same Q.

imports.name: Attached
imports.text: Attached(P, ρ, j) takes a family of complex polynomials P_w indexed by the finite places of the CM field E, a representation ρ of a group H with a topology on an n-indexed vector space over the algebraic closure of ℚ_ℓ, and a map j from H to Gal(Ω/E). For H = Gal(Ω/E), j defaults to the identity. The representation is continuous, the trace pairing (X,Y) ↦ tr(XY) is nondegenerate on the linear span of ρ(H), and j is open. For every real η > 0, for most geometric Frobenius data (w,A,s), for every x in H with j(x) = s and every index i, the ℓ-adic distance between coefficient i of the characteristic polynomial of ρ(x) and coefficient i of ι_ℓ(P_w) is at most η. Here most means that each nonempty open subset of Gal(Ω/E) contains a nonempty open subset O such that, outside finitely many w, every Frobenius datum at w with s in O satisfies this condition.

  IsFiniteTypeAt r A ∧ HasJumpsAt r A (jumps κ (Fintype.card n)) ∧

  ℓ = 1 → (r s).1.det = Q.roots.prod)) (c * ∏ l, (X - C (charName T (χ l)).1) ^ t l) := by
imports.text: If r is attached to an eigenform f with label c, characters χ_l and block sizes t_l at split w: above w, r has finite type, the jumps of κ, and IsLabelledAt holds for c·∏(X − x_{χ_l})^{t_l}. The relation to the literature is the second reader's (literature).

literature.verdict: The books and papers give parameter compatibility; the compact squarefree-label predicate needs a separate identification
literature.comparison: Take an eigenform f on the standard definite unitary group of nonzero rank over a CM field with Weil data, a split place w, A over w and an attached r. The product-label hypothesis explicitly requires a monic squarefree nonzero-constant term label c of degree d, separability of c∏(X−xχ) before multiplicities, d+Σt_i=|n|, and a local representation-label condition. The conclusion gives local finite type (finite inertia away from ℓ or potentially crystalline above ℓ), the weight jumps at embeddings above ℓ, and the labelled predicate for c∏(X−xχ)^t. This predicate tests only inertia elements s with the specified tame exponent a of level d!, and forms Q by transforming the roots using ι(T^a). Away from ℓ it requires Q(r(s))=0 and det r(s)=∏roots Q. Above ℓ it uses linear period Frobenius for the Weil pair. Taylor–Yoshida concerns v∤ℓ. BLGGT II, Theorem 1.1 at v|ℓ, gives equal semisimplifications with a monodromy bound, strengthened to Frobenius-semisimplified equality under Shin-regularity. The comparison papers start with eligible GL automorphic representations. Identifying the project's finite Green label and torus characters with the normalized local parameter and passing through its restricted definition of attachment and its period ring requires further results. The compact source uses cyclic base change and the eigencharacter comparison. A statement for arbitrary Frobenius here would exceed the literal labelled predicate.
sources: T. Barnet-Lamb, T. Gee, D. Geraghty and R. Taylor, Local-global compatibility for ℓ=p, II, Ann. Sci. ENS 47 (2014), §1, Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, p. 170. The ordering gives equal semisimplifications and bounds monodromy. Full Frobenius-semisimplified equality is stated at Shin-regular weight. <https://www.numdam.org/item/ASENS_2014__47_1_165_0.pdf#page=7>

R. Taylor and T. Yoshida, Compatibility of local and global Langlands correspondences, Theorem A, J. Amer. Math. Soc. 20 (2007), pp. 467–468, author preprint p. 1. The local representation is Frobenius-semisimplified and carries the paper's dual and |det| twist. <https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0412357#page=1>

Pinned definition of HasProductLabel, including separability and the block ranks. <https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/blob/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact/src/Lib/GaloisRep/LocalGlobal/ParahoricTypeLabel.lean#L22-L29>

IsTameExponent requires s in inertia and IsLabelledAt quantifies through this predicate. <https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/blob/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact/src/Lib/GaloisRep/LocalGlobal/TameExponent.lean#L19-L32>

Pinned definitions of good type, finite type, jumps and PolyKillsAt in the two residue-characteristic cases. <https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/blob/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact/src/Lib/GaloisRep/Main/LocalEmbedding.lean#L27-L53>

structure Data (P : Parameters) where
  /-- `logX = log x`, `logB = log b`, `logX₁ = log x₁`: the sizes are chosen on the logarithmic
  scale. -/
  (logX logB logX₁ : ℝ) (s m r : ℕ) s_le : s ≤ 32 * logX
  thick : Finset _
  g : Fin 2 → ℕ
  piG : 𝓞 P.K
  scale : 1e12 * P.c ≤ log logB ∧ 100 * log logB ≤ logX ∧ 1e6 * logX ≤ logX₁ ∧ 1e6 * logX₁ ≤ logB ∧
    6 * log logX₁ ≤ log logB
  m_mem : ↑m ∈ Icc (exp (logX / 2)) (2 * exp (logX / 2))
  r_mem : ↑r ∈ Icc (exp (5 * logX)) (3 * exp (5 * logX))
  m_pow : ∃ e, m = 2 ^ (e + 1) ∧ s = (e + 1) * 22
  r_pow : ∃ e, r = 3 ^ (e + 1)
  thick_eq_neg_one_mod {m} (d : m ∣ P.N₁ s) : m ∣ P.N₀ * 3 ^ (.log 3 s + 5) → ∀ σ ∈ thick, P.placeClass d σ = -1
  three_term : let φ := P.placeClass P.two_pow_dvd_N₁; ∀ i j, 0 < i → i < j → j ≤ 324 * s →
         ∀ σ ∈ thick, ∀ τ ∈ thick, ∀ ρ ∈ thick, φ (τ / σ) ^ j = φ (ρ / σ) ^ i → φ (τ / σ) = 1
  g_prime i : (g i).Prime
  g_modEq_one i : g i ≡ 1 [MOD P.N₁ s * P.d]
  dvd_g_sub_one i : P.Mω s ^ 2 ∣ g i - 1
  g_injective : g.Injective
  g_mem i : ↑(g i) ∈ Icc (exp logB ^ 10) (exp logB ^ 11)
  norm_piG : piG * star piG = g 0 * g 1
  exists_prime_window : ∀ U ∈ Icc (100 * logB) (2 ^ s), ∃ p, p.Prime ∧ p ≡ 1 [MOD P.Mω s ^ 2] ∧
    log p ∈ Icc U (U + √logB)
imports.text: For parameters P, admissible data: real numbers logX, logB, logX₁ (the logarithms of the scales x, b, x₁), natural numbers s, m, r, a finite set thick of infinite places, two primes g₀, g₁ (g : Fin 2 → ℕ) and an integer π_G of K, with: s ≤ 32 log x; the scale inequalities 10¹²·c ≤ log log b, 100 log log b ≤ log x, 10⁶ log x ≤ log x₁, 10⁶ log x₁ ≤ log b, 6 log log x₁ ≤ log log b; e^{log x/2} ≤ m ≤ 2e^{log x/2}; e^{5 log x} ≤ r ≤ 3e^{5 log x}; m = 2^{e+1} with s = 22(e+1); r a power of 3; the thick places have class −1 modulo the relevant divisors of N₁ and satisfy a three-term condition; each g_i is prime, ≡ 1 mod N₁d, with M_ω² ∣ g_i − 1; g₀ ≠ g₁ (g_injective); b^{10} ≤ g_i ≤ b^{11}; π_G·π̄_G = g₀g₁; and in every window [U, U + √log b] of log p with 100 log b ≤ U ≤ 2^s there is a prime p ≡ 1 mod M_ω².

literature.comparison: Fix a number field K, w finite, a place A of the closure over w, and the project's topological pro-Galois group Γ acting on that closure. For n natural (including zero) and q=(Nw)^n the literal hypothesis IsFrob A q g⁻¹ says that g⁻¹ acts as the qth power on residues. The output x in K_w^× has v(x)=exp(−n) and geometric Artin image [g] in the abelianized decomposition group. As v(π)=exp(−1), the ordinary additive order of this x is +n. Serre takes arithmetic Frobenius F, uniformizers mapping to F on the unramified quotient, and identifies units with abelian inertia. literature.verdict: A simultaneous unit lift and primitive residue derived from two local reciprocity assertions
literature.comparison: For A over the finite place w of K in the Galois closure setup, the project chooses an inertia element γ whose Kummer action has exact order n on a suitable uniformizer radical for every n prime to the residue characteristic. Lean produces a single u in K_w^×, together with proof it is an integral unit, such that its geometric local Artin image equals the class of this particular γ, every residue-field unit is an integral power of its reduction, and v(u)=1. This does not prescribe which primitive residue to use. Surjectivity from units onto abelian inertia gives the first condition. To obtain the second for the same lift, apply the prime-to-p Kummer formula to a (Nw−1)st root of a uniformizer. Serre's arithmetic symbol for (π,u) gives the inverse residue for n=Nw−1. Inversion of reciprocity in Lean gives the residue of u, and the chosen generator forces its exact order Nw−1. This use of the tame symbol is essential even after unit surjectivity.

This includes a primitive 5040th root of unity, the splitting character with its inert sign, an imaginary element satisfying the positivity and integrality conditions, and the finite self-duality idele. AttachedDefs.lean:16–19 requires continuity, nondegeneracy of the trace pairing on the image algebra, openness of the identity map, and for every η>0 eventual coefficientwise distance ≤η on mostFrobenii. The last filter uses prime-norm w and passage to a smaller nonempty open subset of each nonempty open Galois set. An exact identity at cofinally many such w suffices. The definite quotient has discrete automorphic spectrum. A nonzero constituent of f has the same almost-everywhere split eigenvalues. Labesse’s Corollaire 5.3 applies because the compact real groups satisfy its sign condition and E contains Q(ζ₅₀₄₀), hence [E⁺:Q]≥2. It gives a weak base change to a sum of discrete GL blocks with the required cohomological infinitesimal character. Chenevier–Harris Theorem 3.2.3 applies directly only to a cohomological conjugate-self-dual cuspidal GL representation. For the possible residual blocks use Mœglin–Waldspurger’s description as strings of twists of cuspidal representations. For a rank-r member τ|det|ᵗ of such a string, τ|det|^(t+(r−n)/2) is regular algebraic because its archimedean parameters are the corresponding subset of the distinct rank-n parameters, shifted to the rank-r integral parity. literature.comparison: For an arbitrary number field K and a finite set S of its finite places, the additive copy of its S-unit group is a finitely generated ℤ-module with rank + 1 = |S| + |InfinitePlace(K)|. Neukirch includes all infinite places in his S. Taking his set to be the Lean S together with those infinite places gives rank |S|+r₁+r₂−1, with a conjugate pair counted once. His kernel consists of the finite group of roots of unity and his logarithmic image is a full lattice of the asserted rank. literature.comparison: For a finite place w of an embedded CM field E containing a primitive 5040th root and any algebraic Hecke character θ, use its already-defined scalar ℓ-adic avatar. At every A above w it has finite type, and at embeddings above ℓ the jumps are minus the transported infinity weights with multiplicity one. For m=0 or 1 and any s with s⁻¹ acting on residues by (Nw)^m, it supplies x with ordinary order +m (v(x)=exp(−m)) and geometric Artin image [s]. The polynomial X−ιθ_w(x) kills s in the project's sense. Away from ℓ this is scalar evaluation on r(s); at ℓ it is evaluation on the associated period Frobenius. Serre's local algebraicity/Hodge–Tate criterion applies to abelian semisimple characters. Conrad B.3 computes labelled weights and B.4 gives crystallinity for a character algebraic on the entire unit group, together with a crystalline Frobenius formula. Potential crystallinity of a locally algebraic character follows after a finite extension eliminating its finite unit factor. One must use the inverse of Conrad's arithmetic reciprocity and translate Hodge–Tate conventions, compare the local factor with the global avatar, and use local reciprocity for x. The compact proof obtains the result via its rank-one spherical case and quadratic descent.

literature.comparison: Given a nonempty open W in the absolute Galois group and a finite set of excluded places, Lean produces a place of prime norm outside that set and a place above it admitting a Frobenius lift in W, with every such lift at that place in W. Choose a coset gU inside W for an open normal subgroup U. Finite Galois Chebotarev supplies a positive-density set with Frobenius conjugate to g in the quotient. Exclude the prescribed places and the degree-greater-than-one places, which have Dirichlet density zero. Conjugating the choice of the place above the prime realizes the specified representative. Inertia acts trivially in the unramified finite quotient, so every Frobenius lift at that chosen place maps to that representative. The conclusion uses no quantitative density.

literature.comparison: Let T be finite free over Z_p with an action of Γ linear over a compatible commutative Z_p-algebra R, with j(Γ)=G_K open in G_p. Assume potential crystallinity and that J gives the Hodge–Tate jumps on restriction of scalars to Z_p. The B_max-coboundary condition of Defs.lean:51–56 cuts out Z_f(T) among maps Γ→T. Lean gives finite generation over Z_p and rank rank(T)+[K:Q_p]·#(u∈J with u<0), with multiplicity. Every kernel element of j fixes the spanning periods. It acts trivially on B_max⊗T and hence on T. The coboundary equation also forces c to descend to G_K. CocycleContinuity.lean:70–72 gives continuity modulo each p^n for c. Applying it to integral coboundaries on a basis gives continuity of the descended representation. On V=T[1/p], a rational cocycle satisfies the B_max condition exactly when its extension of Q_p by V admits an invariant lift of 1 over B_max. Colmez III.4 identifies these invariant spaces with those over B_cris, including for the extension. Thus this is the Bloch–Kato finite local condition. Corollary 3.8.4 gives dim H¹_f=dim(D_dR/Fil⁰)+dim H⁰. Adding the coboundary dimension dim V−dim H⁰ gives the cocycle dimension. Fontaine III §3.8(i) and the filtered frame in CocycleContinuity.lean:18–23 give dim_Qp(D_dR/Fil⁰)=[K:Q_p]·#(u<0) in this jump convention. Compactness scales every continuous rational cocycle into T. Finitely many coordinate evaluations separate the finite-dimensional rational space and embed Z_f(T) into a finite power of Z_p, giving finite generation. These steps account for the integral, open-image and cocycle formulations.

literature.comparison: Let K be totally complex and let Γ realize the full pro-Galois action on the closure Ω. The target C is a group with a T₁ topology. Even continuity of its group operations is absent from the hypotheses. The given homomorphism θ from the finite idèles is continuous and kills principal finite idèles. Lean produces a continuous group homomorphism μ from Γ satisfying μ(g)=θ(x) whenever Art(x) is the abelianized class of g. Milne V.5.7(a) identifies the kernel on full idèles as the closure of the product of the principal idèles with the connected factors at infinity. Here every infinite factor is connected, so Art on the finite idèles is onto, with kernel the closure of the principal finite idèles. The kernel of θ is closed by continuity and the T₁ hypothesis. Thus θ factors through the quotient, continuously by the quotient-map property, and pulling back along Γ to its abelianization supplies μ. The Lean statement selects a factor, with no separate family of norm compatibilities among its premises.

The archimedean part of u is unconstrained by the conclusion. Serre proves field Hilbert 90. Separate choices of arbitrary local solutions require a restricted-product argument to give an idèle: at almost all unramified nonsplit places the norm-one component is a unit and a solution can be scaled by a base-field uniformizer to become a unit. At split pairs one may put a component on one factor and 1 on the other. Milne proves H¹(G,I_E)=0 for the full idèles, including unit cohomology outside finitely many places. Apply it to the order-two conjugation and project a solution to the finite factors. This directly accounts for the restricted product in the Lean statement.
sources: J.-P. Serre, Local Fields, X §1, Proposition 2, p. 150, and cyclic corollary, p. 151. The coefficient group here is a field's multiplicative group. <https://doi.org/10.1007/978-1-4757-5673-9>

J. S. Milne, Class Field Theory, VII §2, Proposition 2.5 and Corollary 2.6(a), pp. 205–206. The idèle cohomology decomposes into local groups, including the unramified integral-unit argument. <https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/CFT.pdf#page=215>

literature.verdict: Central idempotence for squarefree character labels, extended by zero and tensor products
literature.comparison: For a finite family of finite fields k_w, a finite matrix index set n and an arbitrary tuple of polynomials c_w, the tensor of the label elements in the group algebra of ∏ GL_n(k_w) has square itself and conjugacy-invariant coefficients. Each local factor is set to zero unless c_w is monic, squarefree of degree |n|, and has nonzero constant term. For a valid label the polynomial roots determine multiplicative-character orbits via a fixed faithful character, each assigned partition (1). Green gives a distinct irreducible character for each such datum, within a classification allowing all partitions. Character orthogonality gives the local central idempotent, since its coefficient at g is Ξ(1)·conj Ξ(g)/|GL|. The tensor product preserves central idempotence. IsCentralProj does not mention an adjoint, irreducibility or primitivity. Self-adjointness in the standard finite group algebra follows separately from the character formula, even when a factor is zero.
sources: J. A. Green, The characters of the finite general linear groups, Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 80 (1955), §8, Theorems 13–14, pp. 441–444, especially Theorem 14 and the degree formula on pp. 443–444. The parameters assign a partition to each Frobenius orbit of multiplicative characters. <https://www.ams.org/tran/1955-080-02/S0002-9947-1955-0072878-2/S0002-9947-1955-0072878-2.pdf#page=42>

I. G. Macdonald, Symmetric Functions and Hall Polynomials, 2nd ed., IV §6, pp. 284–286, including (6.5) and the hook-length computation (6.6). <https://math.berkeley.edu/~corteel/MATH249/macdonald.pdf#page=295>

literature.verdict: Standard definite-unitary specialization of automorphic attachment, with polynomial annihilation at spherical places
literature.comparison: Over an embedded CM field E with CM type and Weil data (including a primitive 5040th root and a splitting character), take any nonempty finite rank and any finite w. Every eigenform of the standard definite group has an attached representation. Attached means continuous, trace-nondegenerate, with coefficientwise ℓ-adic approximation to the prescribed Hecke polynomials in the project's mostFrobenii filter. Every attached r satisfies, when the full local maximal compact fixes f, unramifiedness away from ℓ or crystallinity above ℓ, and the prescribed jumps above ℓ. The additional Hecke-polynomial clause is conditional on HasHeckePolyAt at a split w. It requires annihilation on a geometric Frobenius away from ℓ, and on period Frobenius above ℓ. Chenevier–Harris Theorem 3.2.3 starts with regular polarized cuspidal GL data and identifies the characteristic polynomial at spherical w|ℓ. BLGGT Theorem 2.1.1 supplies full away-from-ℓ parameter compatibility and crystalline/jump assertions. Labesse Corollaire 5.3 supplies weak base change, generally an isobaric sum. Transport between unitary eigenforms, GL constituents and the specified weights is necessary. Within that correspondence the polynomial annihilator and the filter notion of attachment retain less than characteristic-polynomial equality and full local compatibility.
sources: G. Chenevier and M. Harris, Construction of automorphic Galois representations, II, Camb. J. Math. 1 (2013), General Hypotheses 1.1, p. 57, Theorem 3.2.3(a′)–(d), pp. 66–67. At a spherical place above ℓ the theorem identifies the characteristic polynomial of crystalline Frobenius. <https://intlpress.com/site/pub/files/_fulltext/journals/cjm/2013/0001/0001/CJM-2013-0001-0001-a002.pdf#page=14>

T. Barnet-Lamb, T. Gee, D. Geraghty and R. Taylor, Potential automorphy and change of weight, Ann. of Math. 179 (2014), Theorem 2.1.1, p. 538, especially clauses (2)–(4). <https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v179-n2-p03-p.pdf#page=38>

J.-P. Labesse, Changement de base CM et séries discrètes, Corollaire 5.3, pp. 43–44 of the author's text. Weak base change gives an isobaric sum and local matching at unramified and split places. <https://webusers.imj-prg.fr/~michael.harris/CBCM.pdf#page=43>
Pinned definitions of Attached and SphericalCompat. <https://github.com/lsernau/grh-lean/blob/72fead102f663d5c7a407964a13dc0cf9d977207/grh-compact/src/Lib/GaloisRep/Main/AttachedDefs.lean#L14-L30>

literature.comparison: K is totally complex, ℓ prime, r and N positive, and an open normal U with a finite family of auxiliary primes satisfies SplitPlaces for m=ℓ^r. This includes m|N, U fixing μ_m and containing inertia off N, pairwise distinct vᵢ away from N with chosen Frobenii φᵢ in U, the prescribed inertia set I away from N and the vᵢ, and generation by the primes above N of class groups of the intermediate fields inside Ω^U. V is a finite discrete module over a commutative ring, killed by m and U-fixed. The element z is central modulo U, has ℓ-adic cyclotomic character 1, and ρ(z)−1 is injective on V. Every m-th root of an N-unit in Ω^U fixed by all φᵢ must be fixed by U. Lean bounds the number of pairs (f,c), where f is V-valued on places over N and infinity, c is continuous and zero on I, and ρ(g)f(x)=f(gx)+c(g). The order is positive and at most |V|^(|ι|+1). Darmon–Diamond–Taylor 2.19 gives a ratio of orders of two Selmer subgroups of H¹ over a number field, in terms of local conditions and H⁰. Identifying the absolute count here needs the local conditions, the numbers of trivializations and coboundaries, and control of the dual contribution via the given root-detection and centrality hypotheses. The published ratio alone does not perform these steps.

literature.verdict: Coefficient descent on a spanning family follows from the integral Amitsur formula.
literature.comparison: For a representation of a B-algebra in matrices over a commutative B-algebra A, the good elements have all characteristic coefficients in the image of B. Assume they span the source over B. Amitsur's formula for a finite sum involves coefficients of products of summands. In characteristic degree j, a word of length at least two occurs with coefficient index strictly below j. Induction in j therefore applies to that product as another element of the algebra. The length-one terms come from the spanning family, with the scalar powers in the image of B. This gives descent without injectivity of the base map, denominators or a characteristic-zero assumption. The Lean conclusion gives no formula for the coefficients.

literature.verdict: Evaluation vanishing follows from the calculation of the finite local condition for twists.
literature.comparison: T is finite free over Z_p with action ρ(g)=χ(j(g))^(−a) for a natural number a. The image j(Γ)=G_K is open. For any integral c satisfying the B_max-coboundary equation for all g, and s with ρ(s)=1, Lean proves c(s)=0, assuming also j(s)∈I_K when a=0. The action already factors through j and its period equation forces c to descend. Tate twists are crystalline and CocycleContinuity.lean:70–72 gives continuity of the descended cocycle. Tensoring with Q_p gives a direct sum of Q_p(−a). Colmez III.4 identifies B_max and B_cris invariants for the finite-dimensional extension defined by c, so the extension has a fixed lift of 1 for either period ring. Bloch–Kato Example 3.9 gives H¹_f(K,Q_p(r))=0 for r<0, so c is a rational coboundary and vanishes wherever ρ(s)=1. For a=0 it gives unramified classes, so the cocycle for the trivial representation vanishes on inertia. In both cases the injection T→T[1/p] gives the integral assertion.

imports.text: If A is finite, killed by n and fixed by Q, and n is prime to the index of Q, then A has Higman's property for Q (some additive τ : A → A has Σ_{g∈G/Q} gτg⁻¹ = 1). The relation to the literature is the second reader's (literature).

literature.verdict: An explicit relative-trace witness from an invertible subgroup index on the coefficient module.
literature.comparison: Let d=[G:Q]. Bézout gives an integer b with bd≡1 mod n. Set τ=b·id on A. Every conjugate of τ equals τ, so the sum over cosets is bd·id=id on the n-torsion module. The input package also asserts that A is finite, Q acts trivially and ρ(z)−m is injective; the construction uses the torsion and coprimality conditions. The result asserts the additive trace witness under the project's definition. The equivalence with relative projectivity of a finite-group representation over a field is the larger classical criterion. G itself in the Lean declaration need only have finitely many Q-cosets.

literature.verdict: explicit finite-level estimate; main-conjecture comparison needs additional arguments
literature.comparison: Fix N≠0, any natural t, and a CM number field E whose specified embedding lands in the Nth cyclotomic field. The theorem produces one positive integer X at most 2^(4(N+t+3)^27) times the class number of E. For every prime ℓ, eligible coefficient ring O, exponent e<t and precision n it bounds the O-length of shaOdd(ℓ,E,O,e,n) by v_O(X). The coefficient ring is a characteristic-zero DVR finite and free over the ℓ-adic integers, with finite quotients and the stipulated roots of unity. The object is a module of locally constant cocycles. At e=0 it imposes vanishing on inertia at ℓ, with no oddness condition. For e>0 it imposes oddness under conjugation and vanishing on the kernel of the cyclotomic character in the decomposition groups at ℓ. Both cases are unramified away from ℓ. The catalogue's t≥1 hypothesis and its unrestricted description as an odd part should be corrected. Greither's Theorem 3.2 identifies an Iwasawa characteristic ideal for character components. Extracting finite-level lengths, the single simultaneous integer and its explicit archimedean size requires additional work. The pinned proof uses a Stickelberger bound, separates e=0 and controls small primes using detecting cocycles. The references give context for this quantitative statement. They do not yet supply an identified printed statement with this uniform bound.

literature.verdict: The weight-zero potentially unramified case of Conrad's local character calculation, with its scalar Weil polynomial.
literature.comparison: Take an embedded number field E, a closure place A, and a continuous character μ:Gal(Ω/E)→Q̄_ℓˣ with finite inertia image at A. The matrix index has one element. Above ℓ the conclusion is potential crystallinity, the single jump 0 at each compatible embedding, and annihilation of the linear Weil operator by X−μ(s) at every compatible Weil pair. Away from ℓ, LocalEmbedding.lean:35–52 reduces finite type to near-identity inertia acting trivially and the polynomial to scalar matrix evaluation. Locally above ℓ, local reciprocity splits μ as a finite-order character on units extended trivially on a uniformizer and an unramified character. Their values lie in a finite coefficient field generated by the inertia values and one Frobenius value. Conrad B.3 computes the weights of the unramified factor from its zero algebraic exponents. B.4(i) makes it crystalline and B.4(ii) computes its Frobenius as the inverse of its value at arithmetic Artin of the uniformizer. Thus the eigenvalue at geometric Frobenius is its character value in the compact convention. The finite factor becomes trivial over a finite extension. On its potentially crystalline period line the Weil action is its original scalar character. Multiplying the two gives μ(s) for all the stated Weil pairs. Finite inertia allows potential crystallinity even when the original finite-order factor ramifies.
